question: In isogenic human iPSC-derived astrocytes, APOE ε3/ε3 cells deposit fibronectin (FN1) at low levels in fibrillar, thread-like arrays, whereas APOE ε4/ε4 cells show elevated FN1 expression and amorphous deposits. In postmortem brain tissue, FN1 strongly colocalizes with AQP4 at the gliovascular interface. Which conclusion is best supported by this pattern?

options.A: APOE ε4 shifts perivascular FN1 toward an amorphous, AQP4-associated deposition pattern because the fibrillar arrangement seen in ε3 cells is replaced by disorganized accumulation at astrocytic endfeet.
options.B: APOE ε4 causes FN1 to relocalize from astrocytes to endothelial cells, which explains why deposits appear at the gliovascular interface in ε4 carriers.
options.C: The amorphous pattern in ε4/ε4 cells reflects a downstream consequence of amyloid-β42 clearance, not a direct effect of the APOE genotype on astrocyte FN1 deposition.
options.D: Because FN1 colocalizes with AQP4, the deposits are produced by the vasculature rather than by astrocytes in APOE ε4 carriers.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Keyed option A correctly integrates two stated premises: (i) isogenic ε3 vs ε4 astrocytes differ in FN1 level and morphology (low/fibrillar vs elevated/amorphous), and (ii) FN1 colocalizes with the astrocytic endfoot marker AQP4 at the gliovascular interface. The conclusion—that ε4 shifts perivascular FN1 toward amorphous, endfoot-associated accumulation—is the most direct integration of these observations.

distractor_analysis.B: The premise that FN1 colocalizes with AQP4 (an astrocytic endfoot marker) is misread as evidence for endothelial production; the premise about elevated astrocytic FN1 in ε4 is contradicted by the relocalization claim.
distractor_analysis.C: The isogenic astrocyte comparison isolates APOE genotype from amyloid-β42, so the elevated/amorphous FN1 deposition cannot be attributed to Aβ42 clearance; the conclusion misattributes the effect.
distractor_analysis.D: AQP4 is an astrocyte marker, so colocalization indicates astrocytic endfoot association, not vascular production; the conclusion contradicts the stated premise.

question: In zebrafish, astroglial overexpression of FN1 is sufficient to induce BBB leakage. In cell and tissue models, FN1 acts through integrin/FAK signaling to suppress VEGFA, reducing endothelial HB-EGF and downstream astrocytic IGF-1. Pharmacological FAK inhibition, integrin β1 blockade (ATN-161), and HB-EGF/IGF-1 supplementation each restore components of the cascade and BBB integrity. If astroglial FN1 expression were knocked down in an APOE ε4 model with established BBB leakage, which outcome would the stated evidence predict?

options.B: BBB integrity would likely improve, because reducing the upstream driver (FN1) should relieve the integrin/FAK-mediated suppression of the VEGFA/HB-EGF/IGF-1 trophic axis that maintains the gliovascular interface.
options.A: BBB integrity would worsen, because FN1 deposition is a protective response to APOE ε4 and its loss would remove a compensatory barrier-reinforcing signal.
options.C: BBB integrity would be unchanged, because the VEGFA/HB-EGF/IGF-1 axis is regulated independently of FN1 and is not the route through which APOE ε4 disrupts the BBB.
options.D: BBB integrity would improve only if amyloid-β42 were also neutralized, because the FN1-driven suppression of VEGFA requires concurrent amyloid-driven inflammation to manifest.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Keyed option B combines (i) the stated sufficiency result—astroglial FN1 overexpression alone is enough to cause BBB leakage—with (ii) the mechanistic chain in which FN1→integrin/FAK→suppressed VEGFA→reduced HB-EGF/IGF-1 produces dysfunction, and each node is rescuable. Reducing the upstream driver should therefore relieve downstream suppression. The rubric allows for partial rescue rather than guaranteed full restoration.

distractor_analysis.A: The evidence that FAK inhibition, integrin β1 blockade, and HB-EGF/IGF-1 supplementation each restore BBB components indicates FN1 is pathogenic, not protective; the conclusion inverts the sign of the dependence.
distractor_analysis.C: The stated mechanistic chain directly links FN1 to the VEGFA/HB-EGF/IGF-1 axis, contradicting the claim of independent regulation.
distractor_analysis.D: The sufficiency experiment (FN1 overexpression alone producing leakage in zebrafish) shows that amyloid-β42 is not required for FN1-driven BBB disruption; the added condition is unsupported.

question: In aged (21–22 month) APOE ε3/ε3 versus APOE ε4/ε4 knock-in mice, cortical FN1 intensity was +98.9% higher in ε4 vessels (P = 4.1×10⁻³⁹, animal-level GEE). Fibrinogen intensity in ε4 vessels was +79.7% higher than in ε3 vessels (P = 1.7×10⁻³). FN1–fibrinogen colocalization was significantly elevated in ε4 brains, and a dextran–Texas Red assay showed increased extravasation in ε4 versus control mice. None of the mice displayed overt amyloid pathology. Which interpretation is best supported by these observations?

options.C: APOE4 drives BBB dysfunction independent of amyloid, because elevated vascular FN1, increased fibrinogen extravasation, greater FN1–fibrinogen colocalization, and dextran leakage all co-occur in ε4 mice without overt amyloid pathology.
options.A: FN1 accumulation in ε4 mice is a downstream consequence of amyloid deposition, because aged ε4 knock-in mice commonly develop amyloid plaques that trigger fibronectin upregulation.
options.B: The dextran–Texas Red leakage result is the decisive evidence, because a single functional permeability assay outweighs the static colocalization and intensity measurements.
options.D: Fibrinogen extravasation is the primary driver of FN1 deposition, because fibrinogen intensity rose +79.7% and so must have preceded fibronectin accumulation.

rubric.correct_reasoning: The conclusion that APOE4 drives BBB dysfunction independent of amyloid is supported by combining (i) the absence of overt amyloid pathology in the knock-in mice, (ii) the parallel increases in FN1 (+98.9%) and fibrinogen (+79.7%) in ε4 vessels, (iii) the elevated FN1–fibrinogen colocalization, and (iv) the independent confirmation by dextran–Texas Red leakage. Option A is the only choice whose conclusion and reasoning both match this chain.

distractor_analysis.A: Wrong conclusion (FN1 attributed to amyloid) and wrong reasoning (assumes amyloid is present, which the stated premise explicitly denies).
distractor_analysis.B: Right concept (leakage matters) but wrong reasoning: elevates one assay above the orthogonal static readouts; the evidence does not license ranking one readout as 'decisive' over the others.
distractor_analysis.D: Direction of causation is reversed with no temporal evidence; a larger fold-change in fibrinogen does not establish that fibrinogen precedes or drives FN1 deposition.

question: Suppose the FN1–fibrinogen colocalization assay in aged ε4 versus ε3 mice had shown no difference between genotypes, while the FN1 intensity (+98.9%), fibrinogen extravasation (+79.7%), and dextran–Texas Red leakage results remained as stated. Given this hypothetical pattern, which conclusion would the original stated evidence most directly support?

options.A: APOE4-associated BBB dysfunction would be ruled out, because colocalization is the only readout that links fibronectin to vessel leakage.
options.D: APOE4-associated BBB dysfunction would still be supported, because the convergence of elevated FN1, elevated fibrinogen extravasation, and dextran leakage independently indicates compromised barrier function even without colocalization evidence.
options.B: FN1 accumulation would be established as amyloid-independent, because colocalization with fibrinogen is what rules out amyloid involvement.
options.C: The genotype effect on FN1 would be invalidated, because without colocalization the +98.9% FN1 increase is artifactual.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Removing the colocalization result does not negate the other three orthogonal readouts: the +98.9% FN1 increase, the +79.7% fibrinogen extravasation, and the dextran–Texas Red leakage each independently point to barrier dysfunction in ε4 mice. The convergence of these remaining premises still supports BBB dysfunction in the absence of amyloid pathology.

distractor_analysis.A: Wrong conclusion: overweights colocalization as the sole evidence for BBB dysfunction, ignoring the other readouts.
distractor_analysis.B: Wrong conclusion and wrong reasoning: amyloid independence is established by the knock-in design and absence of amyloid pathology, not by fibrinogen colocalization.
distractor_analysis.C: Wrong conclusion: dropping one supporting readout does not invalidate an FN1 intensity measurement that was quantified at the animal level (GEE).

question: In a single-nucleus RNA-seq analysis of 413,175 brain cells from 52 individuals, 19,387 cells expressed FN1 (4.7%). Astrocytes accounted for 22.7% of these FN1-expressing cells, excitatory neurons for 32.68%, and endothelial cells plus pericytes together for 8.9%. Astrocytes comprise ~40% of all brain cells and nearly all contact the vasculature, whereas endothelial cells and pericytes together represent only 2–4% of brain cells. Based on these observations, which conclusion is best supported?

options.B: Excitatory neurons are the predominant source of pathological perivascular FN1 deposition because they constitute the largest share of FN1-expressing cells (32.68% vs. 22.7% for astrocytes).
options.C: Endothelial cells and pericytes are the predominant contributors to pathological perivascular FN1 deposition because the 8.9% of FN1-expressing cells in those lineages reflects a high per-cell FN1 production rate.
options.A: Astrocytes are the predominant contributors to pathological perivascular FN1 deposition despite representing only 22.7% of FN1-expressing cells, because their ~40% abundance, near-universal vascular contact, and demonstrated APOE ε4-dependent FN1 upregulation together favor perivascular protein accumulation.
options.D: Astrocytes cannot be the predominant source because astrocytes account for fewer FN1-expressing cells than excitatory neurons, and a larger fraction of expressing cells always implies a larger contribution to protein deposition.

rubric.correct_reasoning: The keyed option correctly combines (i) the stated observation that astrocytes are 22.7% of FN1-expressing cells with (ii) their ~40% abundance, (iii) near-universal vascular contact, and (iv) APOE ε4-dependent FN1 upregulation, concluding that astrocytes predominate at the perivascular interface despite a smaller share of FN1-expressing cells than excitatory neurons. This matches the paper's argument that pathological ECM deposition depends on abundance plus localization plus APOE ε4-dependent upregulation, not simply the proportion of FN1-expressing cells.

distractor_analysis.B: The conclusion is wrong because it assumes that the largest fraction of FN1-expressing cells implies the predominant source of perivascular protein deposition, ignoring that excitatory neurons are not predominantly perivascular and that the data do not show excitatory-neuron FN1 protein upregulation with APOE ε4.
distractor_analysis.C: Both conclusion and reasoning fail: the 8.9% of FN1-expressing cells that are endothelial/pericyte is a compositional proportion, not a per-cell production rate, and the endothelium/pericyte fraction of brain cells (2–4%) is far smaller than the astrocyte fraction (~40%), so the data do not support their predominance.
distractor_analysis.D: The reasoning fails because it asserts a universal rule (larger fraction of expressing cells = larger contribution to deposition) that the data and the stated biology explicitly contradict; a perivascular lineage with lower mRNA fraction but higher abundance and localization can dominate ECM deposition.

question: snRNA-seq of 424 DLPFC samples (1.64 million nuclei) identified astrocyte cluster 5 (SERPINA3⁺, inflammatory) as the cluster most strongly associated with FN1 in AD (β = 0.0300, FDR P = 1.55×10⁻⁶). Label transfer to an independent dataset showed this reactive subcluster expressed FN1 in the highest proportion of cells, and an independent snRNA-seq analysis showed astrocytes display the highest APOE ε4-dependent FN1 upregulation. Multiplex immunostaining of 1,098,338 cells further showed that APOE ε4/ε4 selectively increases astrocytic FN1 protein. If the SERPINA3⁺ astrocyte cluster 5 were removed from the dataset, which statement about FN1 deposition at the gliovascular interface is most consistent with these observations?

options.A: FN1 deposition at the gliovascular interface would be unchanged, because total astrocyte abundance (~40%) would still exceed other perivascular lineages and is the sole determinant of deposition.
options.B: FN1 deposition at the gliovascular interface would be substantially reduced, because the observations pin the FN1-associated AD signal specifically to cluster 5 and link its upregulation to APOE ε4, indicating this reactive subcluster is a key source of the APOE ε4-driven perivascular FN1.
options.C: FN1 deposition at the gliovascular interface would increase, because removing inflammatory cluster 5 would eliminate competition for the FN1 transcript among astrocytes.
options.D: The outcome cannot be inferred in either direction, because the β of 0.0300 reflects variance explained rather than a directional effect and therefore does not license a counterfactual prediction.

rubric.correct_reasoning: The keyed option chains three premises from the stem: (i) cluster 5 has the strongest FN1–AD association (β = 0.0300, FDR P = 1.55×10⁻⁶), (ii) label transfer independently places FN1 expression highest in this subcluster, and (iii) APOE ε4 selectively upregulates astrocytic FN1 protein. The counterfactual (removing cluster 5) is asked in the direction the evidence identifies — reducing the specific subcluster tied to APOE ε4-driven FN1 would substantially reduce perivascular FN1 deposition. This is a directed counterfactual grounded in the stated evidence.

distractor_analysis.A: The reasoning is wrong because total astrocyte abundance (~40%) is not the sole determinant; the evidence specifically ties the AD-relevant FN1 signal to cluster 5 and to APOE ε4-dependent upregulation, so removing that subcluster would not leave deposition unchanged.
distractor_analysis.C: The conclusion is wrong; nothing in the data supports the idea that inflammatory cluster 5 competes with other astrocytes for FN1, and removing a positive source cannot increase deposition.
distractor_analysis.D: The reasoning misreads β = 0.0300. β in this regression context is a directional effect estimate for the FN1–AD association in cluster 5, not R² or variance-explained; a positive, genome-wide significant β combined with label-transfer and protein-level evidence does license a directional counterfactual.

question: In a 3D primary human astrocyte (pHA) hydrogel system, TNF treatment increased reactive markers (SERPINA3, SAA1), NF-κB signaling, and FN1 expression, while IL-4 reduced FN1 on its own and after TNF or Aβ42 treatment. Separately, snRNA-seq of ~1.64 million nuclei from 424 ROSMAP dorsolateral prefrontal cortex samples identified reactive astrocyte cluster 5 (SERPINA3+) as the cluster most strongly associated with FN1 levels. Based on these stated findings, which interpretation is best supported?

options.A: FN1 deposition is uniquely driven by IL-4 because IL-4 reduced FN1 both alone and after TNF or Aβ42 treatment, whereas TNF only increased it. Because IL-4 reversed multiple inducers, it acts as the obligatory upstream regulator of astrocytic FN1. Because IL-4 reversed multiple inducers, it acts as the obligatory upstream regulator of astrocytic FN1.
options.C: The data support inflammation—via TNF and downstream NF-κB signaling—as a driver of astrocytic FN1 deposition. Because both TNF and Aβ42 induce FN1 and IL-4 reduces it across conditions, and SERPINA3+ reactive astrocytes are the FN1-associated cluster, inflammatory signaling (not IL-4 alone) is implicated as the convergent upstream input. Because IL-4 counteracts the FN1-inducing cytokines, inflammatory signaling is implicated as the convergent upstream input.
options.B: TNF must act downstream of IL-4 because IL-4 reduced FN1 after TNF pretreatment, indicating IL-4 overrides TNF signaling. Because reversing an induced phenotype implies the reversing agent is downstream, TNF functions downstream of IL-4 in this axis. Because reversing an induced phenotype implies the reversing agent is downstream, TNF functions downstream of IL-4 in this axis.
options.D: These experiments show that inflammation is not relevant in vivo because they used a 3D hydrogel and cultured astrocytes, not brain tissue. Because the in vitro manipulations cannot be compared with the snRNA-seq P-values from human cortex, the inflammatory findings fail to generalize to AD. Because the in vitro manipulations cannot be compared with the snRNA-seq P-values from human cortex, the inflammatory findings fail to generalize to AD.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Option B is keyed. It combines two premises: (i) TNF and Aβ42 induce FN1 while IL-4 reduces FN1 across conditions (so FN1 is inflammation-responsive), and (ii) the SERPINA3+ reactive cluster is the FN1-associated cluster in human cortex snRNA-seq. From these, it concludes that inflammation (TNF/NF-κB) — not IL-4 alone — is the convergent upstream driver. This matches the paper's conclusion that inflammation is a major driver of fibronectin deposition.

distractor_analysis.A: Conclusion fails. The data show TNF increases FN1 and IL-4 decreases it; this does not mean IL-4 is the 'obligatory upstream regulator' — sufficiency of IL-4 to reduce FN1 does not establish necessity or uniqueness. The reasoning overinterprets a rescue as obligatory gating. Also the claim that IL-4 is 'unique' misreads the comparison: TNF also drives FN1.
distractor_analysis.B: Conclusion and reasoning both fail. Reversing an induced phenotype does not place the reversing agent downstream; IL-4 antagonizing TNF-induced FN1 is consistent with IL-4 acting in an opposing pathway, not downstream of TNF. This is a fundamental misreading of counteracting interventions.
distractor_analysis.D: Conclusion fails. The paper explicitly integrates in vitro 3D pHA, snRNA-seq from human cortex, postmortem immunolabeling (FN1–GFAP r = 0.9177), and zebrafish in vivo work — so the in vitro findings are not dismissed. The reasoning also misapplies the rule against combining different baselines by treating it as a reason to discard an entire line of evidence rather than to note non-comparability of specific numbers.

question: In ROSMAP dorsolateral prefrontal cortex snRNA-seq (~1.64M nuclei, 424 samples), astrocytic NF-κB1 expression was higher in AD, with a stronger increase in APOE ε4 carriers (P < 0.0001). Donor-averaged regression showed NF-κB2 expression strongly predicted astrocytic FN1 levels (β ≈ 0.44, P = 2.4 × 10⁻²¹). In zebrafish, TNF injection induced fibronectin deposition around astroglia concomitant with NF-κB:GFP activation, and the anti-inflammatory compounds camptothecin and Torin2 reversed amyloid-induced FN1 deposition and astrocytic hypertrophy. Given this pattern, which inference is most defensible?

options.A: Because NF-κB1 shows P < 0.0001 in AD and NF-κB2 predicts FN1 with P = 2.4 × 10⁻²¹, NF-κB1 must be upstream of NF-κB2 in the signaling cascade. Because the NF-κB2 P-value is smaller than the NF-κB1 P-value, NF-κB1 lies upstream of NF-κB2 by definition of pathway architecture. Because the NF-κB2 P-value is smaller than the NF-κB1 P-value, NF-κB1 lies upstream of NF-κB2 by definition of pathway architecture.
options.D: The findings are consistent with inflammation—specifically TNF/NF-κB signaling—being sufficient to drive astrocytic FN1 deposition. Because TNF induces FN1 in 3D pHA and zebrafish with NF-κB activation, NF-κB2 predicts astrocytic FN1 in human cortex, and anti-inflammatory compounds reverse amyloid-induced FN1 in vivo, inflammation is sufficient to drive FN1 deposition. Because TNF induces FN1 in 3D pHA and zebrafish with NF-κB activation, NF-κB2 predicts astrocytic FN1 in human cortex, and anti-inflammatory compounds reverse amyloid-induced FN1 in vivo, inflammation is sufficient to drive FN1 deposition.
options.B: Because camptothecin and Torin2 rescue amyloid-induced FN1 deposition, these compounds must act by directly blocking astrocytic NF-κB signaling. Because the rescue phenotype is observed, the molecular target must be astrocytic NF-κB. Because the rescue phenotype is observed, the molecular target must be astrocytic NF-κB.
options.C: Because APOE ε4 carriers show a stronger NF-κB1 increase (P < 0.0001) than non-carriers, APOE ε4 is necessary for inflammation-driven FN1 deposition in AD. Because the genotype modifies the inflammatory signal, it is the obligatory gate for this pathway. Because the genotype modifies the inflammatory signal, it is the obligatory gate for this pathway.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Option B is keyed. It chains three stated premises: (1) TNF induces FN1 with NF-κB activation in 3D pHA and zebrafish; (2) NF-κB2 predicts astrocytic FN1 in human cortex (β ≈ 0.44); (3) anti-inflammatory compounds (camptothecin, Torin2) reverse amyloid-induced FN1 in vivo. Together these show that inflammatory/NF-κB signaling is sufficient to drive astrocytic FN1 deposition. The conclusion uses 'sufficient to' rather than 'necessary/obligatory', which is what the evidence licenses.

distractor_analysis.A: Reasoning fails. A smaller P-value does not indicate upstream or downstream position in a pathway; P-values reflect effect size, variance, and sample size. The paper does not establish ordering of NF-κB1 vs NF-κB2, so claiming NF-κB1 is upstream based on P-value magnitude is a category error.
distractor_analysis.B: Conclusion and reasoning fail. The paper states camptothecin and Torin2 promote anti-inflammatory states by modulating microglial polarization — i.e., they act via microglia, not by directly blocking astrocytic NF-κB. Inferring direct astrocytic NF-κB blockade from a rescue phenotype is unwarranted.
distractor_analysis.C: Conclusion fails. A stronger NF-κB1 increase in ε4 carriers shows APOE ε4 amplifies the inflammatory signal; it does not establish necessity. Necessity would require loss of FN1 induction when APOE ε4 is absent in a properly controlled experiment, which is not what these data show. The reasoning conflates 'amplifies' with 'obligatory gate'.

question: In isogenic iPS cell-derived astrocytes, APOE ε4/ε4 cells show a 163.6% higher APOE protein signal (P = 1.6 × 10⁻²¹) and stronger APOE–FN1 colocalization (R² = 0.396 vs 0.049 in ε3/ε3). Postmortem ε4/ε4 AD brains confirm elevated APOE (+64.9%, P = 7.3 × 10⁻³) and FN1 (+30.6%, P = 1.9 × 10⁻²). Which interpretation is best supported by these findings?

options.B: ε4/ε4 astrocytes synthesize more APOE than ε3/ε3 astrocytes, because the measured APOE protein signal is significantly higher in ε4/ε4 cells. Because the higher APOE co-occurs with more FN1, APOE likely drives FN1 deposition directly.
options.A: ε4/ε4 astrocytes accumulate APOE intracellularly and perivascularly, because elevated APOE signal combined with the known secretion deficit of ε4 indicates retention rather than increased production. The parallel FN1 increase places both proteins at the gliovascular interface without implying direct interaction.
options.C: FN1 drives the elevated APOE signal in ε4/ε4 astrocytes, because APOE and FN1 show higher colocalization in ε4/ε4 than in ε3/ε3 and FN1 was efficiently immunoprecipitated from astrocyte media.
options.D: The data rule out any functional relationship between APOE and FN1, because co-immunoprecipitation failed to detect a direct APOE–FN1 complex in astrocyte media and lysates.

rubric.correct_reasoning: The keyed option correctly notes that the elevated APOE signal in ε4/ε4 reflects perivascular/intracellular accumulation rather than increased synthesis (consistent with the authors' interpretation that impaired ε4 lipidation and secretion cause retention). It also notes that the parallel FN1 increase places both proteins at the gliovascular interface without requiring a direct interaction — directly matching the stated observations.

distractor_analysis.B: Fails on the reasoning: elevated signal is not evidence of increased synthesis, since the authors explicitly attribute it to impaired secretion/retention. Also overstates causality by claiming APOE 'directly' drives FN1 deposition despite no co-IP evidence.
distractor_analysis.C: Fails on the conclusion: directionality is reversed. FN1 was successfully immunoprecipitated, but APOE was not detected in FN1 pulldowns, so there is no evidence that FN1 drives APOE elevation.
distractor_analysis.D: Fails on the conclusion: a negative co-IP rules out a stable direct binary interaction under those conditions but does not exclude indirect associations, co-localisation through a third partner, or any functional relationship — as the authors themselves state.

question: APOE ε4/ε4 astrocytes show stronger APOE–FN1 colocalization (R² = 0.396 vs 0.049) and elevated APOE (+163.6%) and FN1 levels in vitro, confirmed in postmortem ε4/ε4 AD brains. Co-immunoprecipitation of FN1 from astrocyte media and lysates successfully pulled down FN1 but did not detect APOE. If FN1 were knocked down in ε4/ε4 astrocytes, what outcome would the stated evidence license predicting?

options.A: APOE signal would fall substantially, because APOE and FN1 colocalize strongly in ε4/ε4 cells, so FN1 likely retains APOE at perivascular sites and FN1 loss would release APOE.
options.B: APOE signal could rise, fall, or remain unchanged, because the stated evidence only shows APOE and FN1 co-accumulate at endfeet without demonstrating that FN1 causally controls APOE levels or retention, since no direct interaction was detected.
options.C: APOE signal would definitely rise, because impaired ε4 lipidation causes APOE retention independently of FN1, and removing FN1 would relieve a co-accumulating burden on the same compartment.
options.D: APOE signal would be abolished, because FN1 and APOE show the strongest colocalization in ε4/ε4 cells (R² = 0.396), implying FN1 is the obligatory anchor for APOE at the gliovascular interface.

rubric.correct_reasoning: The stated evidence shows co-accumulation and colocalization but provides no demonstration that FN1 causally controls APOE levels or retention. The negative co-IP rules out direct binding and the authors explicitly state impaired lipidation/secretion drives APOE retention. Without a necessity test (e.g., FN1 knockdown with APOE measurement), the direction of any FN1-loss effect on APOE is undetermined.

distractor_analysis.A: Fails on the conclusion: the evidence does not establish FN1 as a retention mechanism for APOE; colocalization alone cannot fix the direction of the counterfactual, and the negative co-IP argues against a direct retention role.
distractor_analysis.C: Fails on the conclusion: the direction is not pinned down by the data. The stated evidence cannot distinguish whether FN1 loss would raise, lower, or leave APOE unchanged.
distractor_analysis.D: Fails on both conclusion and reasoning: 'abolished' and 'obligatory anchor' vastly overstate the evidence. A correlation (R² = 0.396) plus co-localisation cannot establish necessity, and the negative co-IP directly contradicts a direct obligate relationship.

question: In zebrafish with fn1b knockout, single-cell transcriptomics across 32,294 cells in 38 clusters showed significant KEGG enrichment of VEGF (P = 3.8×10⁻², OR = 2.87), insulin (P = 4.3×10⁻³, OR = 35.78), and MAPK (P = 4.0×10⁻⁵, OR = 3.41) pathways, and astrocytes specifically upregulated vegfa. In human samples, VEGFA protein was 12.3% lower in AD versus control brains (P = 3.7×10⁻¹⁶) and 19.4% lower in APOE ε4/ε4 versus isogenic ε3/ε3 iPSC-derived astrocytes (P = 3.6×10⁻¹⁰). Culturing APOE ε3/ε3 astrocytes on fibronectin-coated plates reduced VEGFA by 25.7% (P = 1.2×10⁻¹⁰). What do these observations collectively indicate?

options.C: Fibronectin signaling through astrocytes suppresses VEGFA, because the same VEGFA reduction is observed in three independent settings: AD brains, APOE ε4/ε4 astrocytes, and ε3/ε3 astrocytes placed on fibronectin-coated plates.
options.A: APOE ε4 is the primary driver of reduced astrocytic VEGFA in AD, because ε4/ε4 astrocytes show a 19.4% reduction while AD brains show only a 12.3% reduction and the ε4 effect is the largest among the three numbers.
options.B: The MAPK pathway is the most upstream regulator of VEGFA in this system, because the smallest P-value (4.0×10⁻⁵) was obtained for MAPK enrichment among the three KEGG pathways.
options.D: VEGFA reduction is a secondary consequence of neuronal loss in AD, because the zebrafish experiment shows pathway enrichment at the whole-brain level rather than in astrocytes alone.

rubric.correct_reasoning: The three independent settings—AD postmortem brain tissue (−12.3%), APOE ε4/ε4 astrocytes versus isogenic ε3/ε3 (−19.4%), and ε3/ε3 astrocytes cultured on fibronectin-coated plates (−25.7%)—all converge on reduced VEGFA. Because plating on fibronectin alone (without any APOE manipulation) phenocopies the ε4 reduction, the common upstream factor is fibronectin engagement, implicating fibronectin signaling through astrocytes as the suppressor of VEGFA.

distractor_analysis.A: Wrong reasoning: it treats the 19.4% vs 12.3% comparison as if it ranks 'driver' status, but these numbers have different baselines (ε3/ε3 isogenic astrocytes vs. control postmortem brains) and combining them across denominators is not licensed. The conclusion that ε4 is 'the primary driver' ignores that FN1 coating in ε3/ε3 cells reproduces the ε4 effect.
distractor_analysis.B: Wrong reasoning: it equates the smallest P-value with the most upstream pathway position. P-value magnitude reflects effect size, variance, and sample size, not position in a cascade; the paper does not establish MAPK as upstream of the FN1–integrin–FAK axis from P-values alone.
distractor_analysis.D: Wrong conclusion: the KEGG enrichment was computed across all clusters from fn1b⁻/⁻ (+Aβ42) versus wild-type (+Aβ42) zebrafish, and the paper specifically highlights that astrocytes in the fn1b knockout upregulated vegfa, directly implicating astrocytic VEGFA regulation rather than neuronal loss.

question: In a model where fibronectin-coated surfaces reduce astrocytic VEGFA by 25.7% (P = 1.2×10⁻¹⁰), treatment with the selective FAK inhibitor PF-573228 restored VEGFA in Aβ42-treated zebrafish and in APOE ε4/ε4 iPSC-derived astrocytes. The independent β-integrin blocker ATN-161 upregulated VEGFA by 20.0% in APOE ε4/ε4 astrocytes (P = 1.0×10⁻⁴). CSF coexpression analysis showed a strong FN1–VEGFA main effect (F = 26.39, P = 2.79×10⁻⁷) and a significant three-way interaction among FN1, APOE ε4 status, and disease status (F = 14.02, P = 1.81×10⁻⁴). Given that blocking β-integrin or its downstream kinase FAK both reverse the VEGFA suppression, what does the pattern of effects most directly support?

options.D: FN1 signaling through integrin–FAK is sufficient to suppress VEGFA, because two independent pharmacological entry points—receptor (β-integrin) and downstream kinase (FAK)—both restore VEGFA when blocked.
options.A: FAK is the obligatory and unique gatekeeper of VEGFA, because PF-573228 restored VEGFA in both zebrafish and human astrocytes and produced the strongest statistical effect.
options.B: APOE ε4 independently reduces VEGFA through a pathway that bypasses integrin signaling, because the FN1–VEGFA three-way interaction only adds ε4 status as a modifier rather than a mediator.
options.C: Aβ42 is the most upstream trigger of VEGFA loss, because PF-573228 restored VEGFA specifically in Aβ42-treated zebrafish rather than in untreated wild-type animals.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Two independent pharmacological interventions converge on the same phenotype: blocking the receptor (β-integrin via ATN-161) and blocking the downstream kinase (FAK via PF-573228) both restore VEGFA that was suppressed by fibronectin engagement. Convergent rescue from independent nodes in the same pathway is the hallmark of a sufficient signaling chain; combining this with the strong FN1–VEGFA main effect licenses the conclusion that FN1→integrin→FAK signaling is sufficient to suppress VEGFA.

distractor_analysis.A: Wrong reasoning: rescue from FAK inhibition shows sufficiency in that context but does not establish that FAK is the obligatory or unique gate. Loss-of-function with residual effect was not tested; necessity cannot be inferred from pharmacological blockade alone.
distractor_analysis.B: Wrong conclusion and reasoning: the FN1–VEGFA three-way interaction (FN1 × APOE ε4 × disease) indicates that the slope of the FN1–VEGFA relationship differs between APOE ε4 carriers with AD and noncarriers/controls, which is consistent with ε4 status modifying the FN1–VEGFA coupling rather than acting through a bypass route. The pharmacology (ATN-161, PF-573228) further argues that ε4 effects route through integrin/FAK signaling.
distractor_analysis.C: Wrong conclusion and reasoning: the paper tested PF-573228 'under Aβ42 conditions' to show rescue of a suppression that fibronectin also produces, but it does not compare untreated versus Aβ42-treated wild-type zebrafish, so Aβ42 cannot be ranked as the most upstream trigger from the stated evidence. The 'strongest statistical effect' language also misuses F statistics.

question: In VEGFR inhibitor (VEGFRi)-treated zebrafish, endothelial hbegf expression is reduced (−28.3%, P = 3.5×10⁻²) and astrocytic igf1 is reduced (−35.2%, P = 6.6×10⁻⁶⁰). In sorted her4:EGFP⁺ astrocytes, recombinant HB-EGF injection induces igf1 expression without changing vegfa levels. These observations together indicate which relationship between HB-EGF and IGF-1 in the VEGF-treated gliovascular niche?

options.B: HB-EGF acts downstream of IGF-1 because VEGFRi reduces both hbegf and igf1 transcripts in the same experiment.
options.C: HB-EGF and IGF-1 are independently regulated by VEGFR signaling because both are reduced by VEGFRi to comparable percentages.
options.A: HB-EGF acts upstream of IGF-1 because VEGFRi lowers hbegf, and adding HB-EGF back to astrocytes selectively raises igf1 without altering vegfa, placing HB-EGF between VEGF signaling and IGF-1 output.
options.D: HB-EGF is a more important trophic signal than IGF-1 because the VEGFRi-induced reduction in hbegf (−28.3%) is larger in magnitude than the reduction in igf1 (−35.2%).

rubric.correct_reasoning: Keyed option A is correct. VEGFRi lowers endothelial hbegf (premise 1), and exogenous HB-EGF raises astrocytic igf1 without changing vegfa (premise 2). Combining these two premises places HB-EGF downstream of VEGFR signaling and upstream of IGF-1: VEGFR → HB-EGF → IGF-1. The selectivity of the HB-EGF effect on igf1 (no change in vegfa) rules out a general transcriptional activation and supports a specific upstream position for HB-EGF relative to IGF-1.

distractor_analysis.B: Wrong conclusion and wrong reasoning. Placing HB-EGF downstream of IGF-1 contradicts the rescue experiment in which HB-EGF addition raised igf1; co-reduction in one experiment does not establish order. The reasoning appeals only to the single premise of parallel downregulation, which is insufficient to infer directionality.
distractor_analysis.C: Wrong conclusion. Independent regulation is inconsistent with the observation that adding HB-EGF raises igf1, which directly couples the two. The reasoning misreads the parallel reductions under VEGFRi as evidence against a pathway rather than as consistent with VEGFR acting through HB-EGF to affect IGF-1.
distractor_analysis.D: Wrong conclusion. The claim about relative importance is not licensed by the data: −28.3% and −35.2% are measured on different transcripts in different cell types, so their magnitudes are not directly comparable. The reasoning commits a cross-baseline magnitude comparison and ignores the actual upstream–downstream evidence from the HB-EGF add-back.

question: In APOE ε3/ε3 human iPSC-derived astrocytes, HB-EGF increases IGF-1 expression in a dose-dependent manner (+73.4%, P = 3.1×10⁻¹²), and coating culture wells with fibronectin reduces IGF-1 (−19.9%, P = 2.8×10⁻⁹). In APOE ε4/ε4 astrocytes, β-integrin blockade with ATN-161 raises IGF-1 (+15.9%, P = 1.1×10⁻⁵). If HB-EGF were no longer able to signal to its receptor on astrocytes in the APOE ε4/ε4 genotype, which outcome would the stated evidence predict about IGF-1 levels, and what experiment within this dataset identifies the upstream position of HB-EGF?

options.A: IGF-1 levels would rise in APOE ε4/ε4 astrocytes because removing HB-EGF signaling would mirror the effect of ATN-161, and the upstream position of HB-EGF is shown by the parallel downregulation of hbegf and igf1 under VEGFRi in zebrafish.
options.B: IGF-1 levels would remain unchanged because fibronectin–integrin signaling in APOE ε4 astrocytes is the dominant suppressor, and the upstream position of HB-EGF is shown by its selective induction of igf1 (not vegfa) in sorted her4:EGFP⁺ astrocytes.
options.C: IGF-1 levels would fall further in APOE ε4/ε4 astrocytes because HB-EGF is the only positive input on IGF-1, and the upstream position of HB-EGF is shown by the −28.3% reduction in endothelial hbegf after VEGFR inhibition.
options.D: IGF-1 levels would rise in APOE ε4/ε4 astrocytes because HB-EGF normally suppresses IGF-1, and the upstream position of HB-EGF is shown by the +73.4% induction of IGF-1 by HB-EGF in APOE ε3 astrocytes.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Keyed option B is correct. The data show that in APOE ε4/ε4 astrocytes, blocking β-integrin signaling with ATN-161 raises IGF-1, demonstrating that integrin signaling in this genotype is a net suppressor of IGF-1. Because HB-EGF is a positive driver of IGF-1 (dose-dependent induction in APOE ε3 astrocytes), removing it would remove a positive input, but the data cannot determine whether the integrin-mediated suppression dominates; the safest licensed prediction is that IGF-1 would not increase (and could fall) because the observed net state in APOE ε4 is integrin-driven suppression. The upstream position of HB-EGF relative to IGF-1 is identified by the experiment in which HB-EGF add-back to sorted her4:EGFP⁺ astrocytes selectively induces igf1 without changing vegfa — a direct perturbation showing HB-EGF acts upstream of IGF-1 and not as a general transcriptional activator.

distractor_analysis.A: Wrong conclusion. Predicting a rise because ATN-161 raises IGF-1 conflates blocking integrin signaling (which removes a suppressor) with removing HB-EGF (which removes a positive driver); these are opposite manipulations. The reasoning also misidentifies the upstream evidence: parallel downregulation under VEGFRi is consistent with a cascade but does not, by itself, demonstrate HB-EGF's upstream position — only the selective HB-EGF add-back does.
distractor_analysis.C: Wrong conclusion. The claim that HB-EGF is the only positive input is not established by the data (no necessity test is reported). Predicting a further fall is an over-strong inference that the evidence does not license. The reasoning partly identifies the upstream experiment (VEGFRi reducing hbegf) but this alone does not prove HB-EGF is the sole or dominant positive input on IGF-1.
distractor_analysis.D: Wrong conclusion and wrong reasoning. HB-EGF does not suppress IGF-1 in the dataset; it induces it (+73.4% in APOE ε3). The reasoning inverts the direction of the HB-EGF effect and cites the induction experiment as evidence for upstream position, when induction alone shows HB-EGF is sufficient but the upstream–downstream relationship is established specifically by the selective effect on igf1 vs vegfa in sorted astrocytes.

question: Zebrafish larvae were injected with a construct placing human FN1 under the her4.1 promoter, which drives expression in astroglia (FN1-T2A-GFP), while control larvae received either empty plasmid or PBS. The FN1-injected larvae showed astroglial GFP signal, elevated fibronectin, and dextran–Texas Red leakage from vessels, whereas both control groups maintained intravascular dextran confinement and showed minimal fibronectin. Which interpretation is best supported?

options.A: The dextran leakage in the FN1 group is a non-specific injection artifact because empty plasmid controls also received an injection yet still retained dextran, suggesting leakage depends on the FN1 transgene beyond just the injection itself.
options.B: The BBB leakage is likely driven by an inflammatory response to the GFP reporter rather than fibronectin, because GFP-positive astroglia were only seen in the leakage group and GFP itself can be immunogenic.
options.C: Astroglial FN1 expression is sufficient to compromise gliovascular barrier integrity, because leakage occurred specifically in larvae carrying the her4.1-driven FN1 construct and not in empty-plasmid or PBS controls that shared the injection procedure.
options.D: The control data are inconclusive because two different control types were used, and dextran confinement in PBS-injected larvae cannot be compared to dextran confinement in empty-plasmid-injected larvae since they have different baselines.

rubric.correct_reasoning: The keyed option combines two premises: (1) leakage appeared only in the FN1-construct group and (2) the two control groups (empty plasmid, PBS) — which differ in injection content — both retained dextran confinement. Because the FN1 transgene is the only variable uniquely present in the leaky group and the injection procedure alone (empty plasmid) does not cause leakage, astroglial FN1 expression is sufficient to compromise the barrier. This matches the authors' stated conclusion.

distractor_analysis.A: Wrong reasoning. The empty-plasmid control actually argues against an injection artifact: it underwent the same injection procedure but did not leak, so leakage tracks with the FN1 transgene, not with injection per se.
distractor_analysis.B: Wrong conclusion and reasoning. GFP fluorescence here marks successful astroglial transgene expression, not an immune trigger; the empty-plasmid group could not be evaluated for GFP in the same astroglial pattern because it lacks the FN1-T2A-GFP cassette, so this confounds expression with reporter identity.
distractor_analysis.D: Wrong conclusion and reasoning. The two controls agree (both intact), strengthening rather than undermining the inference; the question does not require combining their results, only noting that neither leaked.

question: In the experiment, her4.1:FN1-T2A-GFP-injected larvae showed astroglial GFP, elevated fibronectin, and dextran extravasation, while empty-plasmid and PBS controls showed neither fibronectin elevation nor dextran leakage. If the astroglial GFP signal in a larva were absent despite injection of the FN1 construct, which conclusion is licensed by the comparison of outcomes?

options.A: The absence of astroglial GFP would prove that the construct failed and that FN1 overexpression is unnecessary for BBB disruption, because leakage has been observed whenever the construct is injected.
options.D: The absence of astroglial GFP would be uninformative about the transgene's role because transgene integration is mosaic and the FN1 construct would still be the only variable shared between leaking and non-leaking larvae.
options.B: The absence of astroglial GFP would imply that astroglial FN1 is neither sufficient nor involved in BBB disruption, because the original conclusion rested on GFP marking the cells that expressed FN1.
options.C: The absence of astroglial GFP would demonstrate that BBB integrity is maintained by a non-FN1 mechanism in those mosaic larvae, because the control groups lacked the construct yet also showed no leakage.

rubric.correct_reasoning: The counterfactual must respect what the evidence licenses. The original comparison identifies astroglial FN1 expression as sufficient — not necessary — to compromise the barrier. A mosaic larva lacking GFP signal (and presumably FN1 in those cells) but otherwise carrying the construct cannot overturn the sufficiency claim, because the construct (not its visible expression in every cell) is the manipulated variable that distinguishes groups. The two stated premises that must be combined: (1) sufficiency does not equal necessity, and (2) construct injection is the group-level variable.

distractor_analysis.A: Wrong conclusion. The original data only demonstrate sufficiency under conditions of astroglial FN1 expression; absence of visible GFP in a mosaic larva does not establish that FN1 is unnecessary.
distractor_analysis.B: Wrong conclusion. The GFP marker aids identification but the experimental variable is the FN1 transgene; the original conclusion depends on the construct/astroglial expression comparison, not on GFP detection in every individual.
distractor_analysis.C: Wrong conclusion. Controls lack the FN1 transgene, so their intact barrier does not identify an alternative maintenance mechanism; it only reinforces that the construct is the variable associated with the phenotype.

question: In brain tissue, VEGFA, HB-EGF, and IGF-1 levels were quantified in three settings: zebrafish AD models, APP knock-in mice, and human Braak V–VI vs. Braak I brains. All three factors were significantly reduced in AD conditions in every species (human: VEGFA P = 9.7 × 10⁻⁸; HB-EGF and IGF-1 P < 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁵; mouse: VEGFA P = 0.016, HB-EGF P = 6.8 × 10⁻⁷, IGF-1 P = 0.0099). In zebrafish parenchymal capillaries, VEGFR inhibition reduced ZO-1/GFP colocalization, and HB-EGF/IGF-1 co-treatment restored tight junction levels. Which interpretation is best supported by this combined evidence?

options.A: The conserved downregulation of VEGFA/HB-EGF/IGF-1 across species indicates that loss of this signaling triad is a core feature of AD pathology, and the rescue of ZO-1 colocalization by HB-EGF/IGF-1 after VEGFR blockade shows this triad is sufficient to maintain endothelial tight junction integrity in vivo.
options.B: The cross-species reduction in VEGFA alone is the dominant driver of AD vascular deficits, because VEGFA shows the largest fold-change reduction in human tissue and the tight junction rescue by HB-EGF/IGF-1 is incidental to the VEGFA effect.
options.C: The ZO-1/GFP rescue experiment in zebrafish is sufficient to conclude that VEGFA is the only obligatory upstream regulator of the triad, since VEGFR inhibition alone abolished tight junction colocalization and adding HB-EGF/IGF-1 bypassed the VEGFA branch entirely.
options.D: Because the P-values for HB-EGF and IGF-1 in human brains are smaller than those for VEGFA in mouse brains, HB-EGF and IGF-1 occupy a more upstream position in the signaling hierarchy than VEGFA in this pathway.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Option A correctly combines two premises: (i) VEGFA/HB-EGF/IGF-1 are significantly reduced across zebrafish, APP knock-in mice, and human Braak V–VI brains, supporting evolutionary conservation of this downregulation in AD; (ii) in zebrafish, VEGFR inhibition reduced ZO-1/GFP colocalization, and HB-EGF/IGF-1 co-treatment restored tight junction levels — a sufficiency test showing that supplying HB-EGF and IGF-1 is enough to rescue tight junction integrity when VEGFR signaling is blocked. The conclusion ('conserved feature of AD pathology' + 'triad is sufficient to maintain tight junctions') is exactly what the evidence licenses.

distractor_analysis.B: Fails on conclusion and reasoning. VEGFA alone is not singled out as the dominant driver; all three factors were significantly reduced across species. Tight junction rescue by HB-EGF/IGF-1 is not incidental — it is the only direct functional rescue demonstrated. Inferring dominance from the largest fold-change is not supported.
distractor_analysis.C: Overreaches. VEGFR blockade plus rescue by HB-EGF/IGF-1 shows that HB-EGF and IGF-1 signaling can be sufficient to restore tight junctions in the absence of VEGFR signaling; it does not establish that VEGFA is 'the only obligatory upstream regulator.' Sufficiency of a rescue is not uniqueness or necessity.
distractor_analysis.D: Compares P-values across species (human HB-EGF/IGF-1 vs. mouse VEGFA) and across different baseline contexts. Even within one species, a smaller P-value reflects effect size/variance/n, not pathway position. This option violates the rule that P-value magnitude cannot be used to rank upstream/downstream position.

question: KEGG enrichment of FN1×APOE4 interaction genes from ROSMAP brain endothelial scRNA-seq identified insulin signaling among negatively regulated pathways in AD. Separately, an mQTL analysis found an intronic FN1 variant (rs2304573) associated with altered VEGFA methylation. In zebrafish, VEGFR inhibition reduced endothelial ZO-1/GFP colocalization and HB-EGF/IGF-1 co-treatment rescued it. What conclusion about fibronectin's role does this combined evidence license?

options.B: Fibronectin and APOE4 alter insulin signaling in the gliovascular niche in AD, and an FN1 variant is associated with VEGFA methylation changes, together suggesting fibronectin contributes to disrupted VEGFA/HB-EGF/IGF-1 signaling in AD.
options.A: Because the FN1 mQTL alters VEGFA methylation and the FN1×APOE4 KEGG set is enriched for insulin signaling, fibronectin is the obligatory upstream cause of every VEGF/IGF-1 deficit observed in AD brain tissue across all three species.
options.C: The negative enrichment of insulin signaling in the FN1×APOE4 KEGG set directly proves that per-cell IGF-1 transcript output is reduced in brain endothelial cells of FN1-high individuals, because enrichment reflects the fraction of expressing cells.
options.D: Since the zebrafish rescue was performed with HB-EGF/IGF-1 co-treatment and not with fibronectin manipulation, the zebrafish data and the human genetics/transcriptomic data are about independent pathways and cannot be linked mechanistically.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Option A chains two stated observations: (i) FN1×APOE4 interaction genes are negatively enriched for insulin signaling in human brain endothelium, and (ii) an FN1 intronic variant associates with altered VEGFA methylation. Together with the zebrafish rescue showing VEGFA/HB-EGF/IGF-1 signaling controls tight junction integrity, these findings are consistent with fibronectin contributing to disrupted VEGF/HB-EGF/IGF-1 signaling in AD. The wording ('contributes to,' 'suggesting') correctly reflects associative evidence and does not overclaim causation.

distractor_analysis.A: Overclaims. mQTL association and KEGG enrichment are associative; they do not establish fibronectin as 'the obligatory upstream cause of every VEGF/IGF-1 deficit.' The zebrafish rescue shows sufficiency of HB-EGF/IGF-1, not that fibronectin is necessary or unique.
distractor_analysis.C: Misinterprets KEGG enrichment. A pathway enrichment from a gene set says nothing about per-cell transcript output. Single-cell compositional fractions are not production rates; this option introduces a forbidden inference.
distractor_analysis.D: Wrong conclusion. The zebrafish data, the FN1×APOE4 enrichment, and the FN1 mQTL all converge on the same VEGFA/HB-EGF/IGF-1 axis — they are not independent pathways. The rescue experiment identifies the axis that fibronectin is proposed to disrupt.

question: In an AD CSF proteomic cohort (n = 156 AD, n = 139 controls), FN1 protein was significantly elevated in AD (t = 5.22, P = 3.31×10⁻⁷), and a gene coexpression analysis showed FN1–VEGFA association (F = 26.39, P = 2.79×10⁻⁷) with a significant three-way interaction among FN1, APOE ε4 status, and disease status (F = 14.02, P = 1.81×10⁻⁴). In the same dataset, controls showed similar VEGFA levels across APOE genotypes, whereas in AD, VEGFA was elevated in non-ε4 carriers but not in ε4 carriers. Plasma FN1 did not correlate with plasma VEGFA (n = 113, r = 0.13). Which interpretation is best supported by these observations?

options.C: The FN1–VEGFA relationship is CNS-specific because in plasma the two proteins showed no correlation while in CSF they were significantly associated, which argues against a systemic source of the co-regulation observed in AD.
options.A: The FN1–VEGFA relationship is systemic because FN1 was elevated in AD CSF and FN1–VEGFA coexpression was detected in the proteomic screen, indicating the proteins track together in every body compartment tested.
options.B: APOE ε4 status is irrelevant to FN1–VEGFA biology in AD because the three-way interaction F statistic (14.02) was smaller in magnitude than the FN1–VEGFA main-effect F statistic (26.39), which means the genotype term contributes less.
options.D: FN1 is unlikely to be a useful AD biomarker because plasma FN1 failed to correlate with VEGFA, and a single null correlation in one compartment is sufficient to disqualify CNS protein measurements from biomarker consideration.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Option A is correct because it integrates two premises: (i) in plasma, FN1 and VEGFA showed no correlation (r = 0.13), and (ii) in CSF they showed a strong association with a significant three-way interaction involving APOE ε4. Together these support CNS-specificity of the FN1–VEGFA co-regulation rather than a systemic origin.

distractor_analysis.A: Wrong conclusion. It claims the relationship is systemic despite the stated plasma data (r = 0.13), contradicting the compartment-specific pattern the observations actually show.
distractor_analysis.B: Wrong reasoning. It compares two F statistics of different model terms and treats the larger F as more biologically important; F values from different model terms are not interchangeable magnitude comparisons, and a smaller F in an interaction term does not make the genotype factor irrelevant — the significant three-way interaction explicitly indicates the FN1–VEGFA slope differs by APOE ε4 in AD.
distractor_analysis.D: Wrong conclusion and reasoning. A null plasma correlation does not disqualify a CNS biomarker; the stem shows CSF FN1 was significantly elevated in AD (t = 5.22), so CSF FN1 itself is the candidate biomarker being evaluated, not the plasma correlation.

question: In an AD CSF proteomic cohort (n = 156 AD, n = 139 controls), FN1 was elevated in AD (P = 3.31×10⁻⁷) and showed a significant three-way interaction with APOE ε4 status and disease status for VEGFA coexpression (F = 14.02, P = 1.81×10⁻⁴). Controls had similar VEGFA levels across APOE genotypes, but in AD, non-ε4 carriers showed elevated VEGFA while ε4 carriers did not. Plasma FN1–VEGFA showed no correlation (r = 0.13). If the compensatory VEGFA increase observed in non-ε4 AD cases were blocked, which prediction is licensed by the stated evidence?

options.D: Blocking VEGFA elevation in non-ε4 AD cases would not affect the FN1 elevation in AD CSF, because FN1 was already significantly higher in AD regardless of APOE genotype, and the interaction concerns VEGFA, not FN1 itself.
options.A: Blocking VEGFA elevation in non-ε4 AD cases would necessarily normalize FN1 back to control levels, because FN1 and VEGFA are coupled and any change in one forces an equivalent change in the other.
options.B: Blocking VEGFA elevation in non-ε4 AD cases would eliminate the APOE ε4 effect on VEGFA entirely, because the absence of VEGFA elevation in ε4 carriers means ε4 carriers would be unaffected by the manipulation.
options.C: Blocking VEGFA elevation in non-ε4 AD cases would abolish the three-way interaction term, because the interaction is defined entirely by the difference in VEGFA slopes between non-ε4 and ε4 AD carriers.

rubric.correct_reasoning: Option A correctly identifies that the three-way interaction (F = 14.02) concerns the FN1–VEGFA slope differing by APOE ε4 in AD, while the main effect of FN1 elevation in AD (t = 5.22, P = 3.31×10⁻⁷) was observed across APOE genotypes. The stated evidence therefore does not support the claim that VEGFA manipulation would reverse FN1 elevation — FN1 elevation is a separate observation from the VEGFA slope difference.

distractor_analysis.A: Wrong conclusion. The evidence shows FN1 elevation in AD regardless of genotype; no stated observation licenses that VEGFA manipulation would force FN1 back to control levels, and the stem does not describe a directional coupling that requires equivalent co-change.
distractor_analysis.B: Wrong conclusion. Eliminating VEGFA elevation in non-ε4 AD would not 'eliminate the APOE ε4 effect on VEGFA' because the ε4 carriers' flat VEGFA slope is itself part of the interaction pattern; the prediction conflates removing one group's elevation with negating the genotype effect.
distractor_analysis.C: Wrong conclusion. The three-way interaction reflects the FN1–VEGFA slope differing by APOE ε4 and disease status; removing VEGFA elevation in non-ε4 carriers would alter but not necessarily 'abolish' the interaction, and the stem does not establish that the interaction is defined entirely by that one difference.
